reader.summary: During the week of October 17 to 24, South Africa's most prominent story was the second Test cricket match against Australia, in which the Proteas staged a dramatic comeback to win by an innings and level the series 1-1. Captain Bavuma scored 179, Jansen took five wickets to enforce a follow-on, and Nortje was ruled out of the third Test. Australia faced selection headaches after what was called a shambolic defeat. In Durban, a foreign national was beaten to death by a mob of roughly 50 people during a protest, reigniting anti-immigrant tensions and prompting a police murder investigation. Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana delivered a mid-term budget featuring a two-month fuel levy cut from November, a new fiscal anchor to rein in government debt, and a framework to bring offshore fund management back onshore. BofA and BNP Paribas signaled potential rating upgrades. President Ramaphosa urged South Africa to prepare for the possible loss of US trade benefits, while trade with China surged after a duty-free deal and Chery selected South Africa to build its Omoda C4. A water-quality crisis near Tshwane sickened over 500 residents, and a shark killed a 65-year-old swimmer off the Eastern Cape. Rugby player Hyron Andrews was confirmed to have died of an aortic dissection.

key_events.event: South Africa beat Australia by an innings in the second Test, leveling the series 1-1, with Bavuma scoring 179 and Jansen taking five wickets.
A foreign national was beaten to death by a mob of approximately 50 people in Durban during a protest, sparking police investigation and renewed anti-immigrant tensions.
Finance Minister Godongwana delivered a mid-term budget introducing a two-month fuel levy cut, a new fiscal anchor, and plans to bring offshore fund management onshore.
President Ramaphosa told South Africa to prepare for the possible loss of US-Africa trade benefits as trade with China surged after a duty-free agreement.
Over 500 residents near Tshwane were sickened in a water-quality outbreak, with authorities declaring tap water undrinkable in the affected area.
A shark killed a 65-year-old woman swimming off the Eastern Cape, prompting the closure of beaches in KuGompo City.
Rugby player Hyron Andrews was confirmed to have died of an aortic dissection, with an emotional tribute paid in France.
Vedanta announced a 600-million-dollar investment to double zinc capacity in South Africa, and IDC neared a 610-million-dollar deal for ArcelorMittal South Africa.
Pick n Pay withdrew its restructuring process after reaching a deal with unions, reporting a narrower interim loss.
BofA and BNP Paribas indicated South Africa could receive a credit-rating upgrade following the budget, and Investec said the country is on a path to investment grade.

In Durban, a crowd of about 50 people beat a foreign visitor to death during a protest. Police are investigating and looking for arrests. Politicians are arguing about immigration, and more protests could happen in other cities.

The government just delivered its mid-year budget with fuel tax cuts and new debt rules. Banks are getting more positive about the economy. At the same time, the country is leaning harder into trade with China, with new car factories and cherry exports heading that way.

The rugby player Hyron Andrews, who died suddenly in France, will drop off the front pages as cricket and women's rugby take over the sports news. A water contamination problem near the capital is getting worse, and that could become a bigger political fight.
